case_study_packaging.headline: Faith-based e-commerce retailer captures $1.24M in annual savings and 13% cost reduction with Treya’s rapid sourcing program
case_study_packaging.client_problem_statement: Christianbook, a 45-year-old omnichannel retailer of Christian books and curricula, managed nearly $18 million in indirect spend through informal, decentralized purchasing practices. Facing margin pressure and aggressive value-creation milestones from sponsor Nonantum Capital Partners, the company needed to quickly uncover meaningful cost reductions without disrupting mission-critical fulfillment operations. Treya Partners was engaged to deliver hard savings, modernize procurement processes, and turbo-charge EBITDA growth.
case_study_packaging.client_problem_anonymized: A long-standing faith-based omnichannel retailer managed nearly $18 million in indirect spend through informal, decentralized purchasing practices. Facing margin pressure and aggressive value-creation milestones from the private equity ownership group, the company needed to quickly uncover meaningful cost reductions without disrupting mission-critical fulfillment operations. Treya Partners was engaged to deliver hard savings, modernize procurement processes, and turbo-charge EBITDA growth.
approach_summary: Analyzed 12-month AP data to baseline $15 million in addressable spend across freight, payments, packaging, and other indirect categories.
Ran competitive RFPs for Merchant Processing and LTL/FTL freight, replacing 30-year incumbent providers and securing fee reductions of 10% and 31%, respectively.
Negotiated incumbent corrugated and packaging suppliers through data-driven should-cost models, capturing 12–14% savings while maintaining service continuity.
Piloted new carrier arrangements during post-peak season to validate service levels before full conversion, de-risking the transition.
Instituted centralized procurement cadence—quarterly business reviews, contract repository, and savings tracking—to embed sustainable practice going forward.
case_study_packaging.value_delivered_blurb: Treya delivered $1,237,359 in recurring annual savings—more than double the guaranteed target and equal to a 13.4% reduction on $9.2 million of baseline spend. The engagement generated an estimated $11 million in enterprise value, producing a 3.3× return on Treya’s fixed project fee. Beyond the dollars, Christianbook gained pricing transparency, expanded supplier bench strength, and a repeatable procurement framework to sustain future savings.
where_we_were_unique: Achieved first implemented savings within 60 days by fast-tracking packaging negotiations.
Surpassed the contractual savings guarantee by 120%, reinforcing Treya’s performance-backed model.
Balanced cost takeout with service continuity—retaining key incumbents where operationally critical while still driving double-digit reductions.
Provided PE-grade analytics and valuation impact, translating run-rate savings into $11 million of enterprise value for stakeholders.

generation_notes: All narrative facts and figures sourced directly from provided data; no assumptions added.
Enterprise value impact estimated using 9× EBITDA multiple cited in impact summary notes.
